node.title: DLI spectral-hypothesis separation no-go
node.statement: Two exact constructions separate the spectral hypotheses in C2''. First, disjoint one-sided frequency sets {2,3} and {4,6} on the order-16 F_17 domain have primitive joint-to-product ratio 8192/485>sqrt(32), because the events mix 2-adic valuation classes. Second, three valuation-pure complete-residue events tensor from local marginal counts 3856,1296,5124 and joint/owner counts 20/4 to ratio C^r(1-5^-r), C=83886080/25006401, exceeding sqrt(64) at r=2; these bands are not globally one-sided. Thus neither one-sidedness nor valuation purity alone suffices. The official nested initial prefix retains both and is not falsified.
node.attack_surface: Check the exact order-16 counts, one-sided and valuation-pure scope labels, primitive subtraction, complete-residue tensorization, field existence, rational constants, and the explicit nonclaim for the conjunction of target hypotheses.
node.falsifier: A mismatch in either exact finite census, an incorrect tensor normalization, or failure of either printed ratio to exceed its square-root threshold.
node.notes: This freezes the minimum viable spectral scope for theorem search: one-sided, valuation-pure, nested initial prefixes with primitive ownership. It does not prove that conjunction sufficient.
